title: Truck bands, brass bands and the district in New Orleans
summary: Joe played on advertising trucks, with hard-boiled eggs for strength, in band contests, with the Onward and Magnolia brass bands, and in district bands at a dollar a night with shared tips.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Oh, yes. I've heard about them.

Yes. And they used to play... If they were going to have a dance, they'd advertise that dance. They'd get on a corner and they'd play, and Joe would play at the top of his voice. And he could hear him for three or four blocks and we'd blow him that horn. Then he had me to fire him around with eggs. Hard-boiled eggs. That always gave him... He said a lot of... In other words, it made him strong. Give him more strength and play. Yes. The hard-boiled eggs.
Did he have a sandwich for him? No, just the eggs.
Just the hard-boiled plain eggs. I'm busy in the kitchen.

And he would take these eggs and he'd go on blowing. They'd get out of the corner and the people would gang around them. Sometimes on Sunday, there were two bands. They'd meet on this corner. And one would try to play the other. Play out the other. That was Celestine. That passed recently. Yes. And all the other bunch.
And it was like a Mardi Gras day. Everybody was out to hear the band.

And Joe was blowing. And after that, he began playing just dances. And he began playing up at Tulane. He organized the band. Did he have his own band? Or had he played with another band, do you know? No, he hadn't played with another band. They would just get musicians here and there. You see, all over New Orleans, they had quite a few musicians. Not like now. He knew all of them and then hardly had a job, standard job. But he would get them up, gather them up and they'd say, we play on Sunday evening. And they would have this truck and they'd go from corner to corner all over town. And they'd say, we played Sunday evening. And they'd have this truck and they'd go from corner to corner all over town. And then after that, Joe organized a band. The first band he played with was a brass band. It was Onward. Onward.
Yes. And the Magnolia. Well, they used to play parades. The Magnolia and Onward both?

Yes. He played with both bands. And they would play street parades like the organization would turn out. And they'd walk for blocks and blocks and blocks just playing music. Well, then after that, as far as I can remember, Joe had a couple of little bands down in the district. He worked down there. They'd get a dollar a night. And we lived beautifully on that dollar a night. During that time.
Did they get tips much in the district? Oh, yes. Oh, yes.
